title: 24 VC Firms Commit ₹1,050 Crore to Deeptech Startups at Bengaluru Tech Summit
excerpt: Commitments announced at the Future Makers Conclave are 2.6 times last year's ₹400 crore, aimed at aerospace, defence, AI, robotics and semiconductor startups — with no disbursement schedule yet shared.
body:
• Twenty-four venture capital firms announced investment commitments totalling ₹1,050.42 crore in deeptech startups at the Future Makers Conclave of the Bengaluru Tech Summit on Thursday.
  • The money is aimed at startups in aerospace, defence technology, AI, robotics, semiconductors, biotechnology and industrial automation, including Dream Aerospace, Agnikul Labs and Asteria Aerospace.
  • The commitments are 2.6 times the ₹400 crore announced at last year's conclave — but they are announcements, not disbursements: no allocation or payout schedule was shared at the event.
  • Named investors include Speciale Invest, Blume Ventures, Rainmatter, Qualcomm Ventures, 3one4 Capital and Avaana Capital.

Twenty-four venture capital firms have announced investments worth approximately ₹1,050 crore in deeptech startups at the Future Makers Conclave 2026, held as part of the Bengaluru Tech Summit on Thursday. The announcements total ₹1,050.42 crore and span startups working in aerospace, defence technology, artificial intelligence, robotics, semiconductors, biotechnology and industrial automation, The Hindu BusinessLine reported.

Companies named among the recipients include Dream Aerospace, Agnikul Labs, Asteria Aerospace, Revy Technologies and Parallel Loop. Among the participating investors are Speciale Invest, Arali Ventures, Avaana Capital, Blume Ventures, Rainmatter (Zerodha), Qualcomm Ventures, 3one4 Capital and AWE Funds, according to the investment details shared at the event.

A step up from last year

The figure marks a significant increase from last year's Future Makers Conclave, where the Karnataka government and venture capital firms together announced ₹400 crore for AI and deeptech startups. One caution applies to both numbers: they are commitments announced at a summit, not money already invested. No disbursement schedule, and no breakdown of how the ₹1,050 crore will be allocated, was provided at the event.

The ecosystem around the announcement

The conclave also highlighted Karnataka's ELEVATE startup support programme, which has backed 1,084 startups so far, including 390 from regions beyond Bengaluru, through funding, mentorship and ecosystem access. Four ELEVATE-supported startups — Curexel, BioAI Innovations, OptM Media Solutions and NSP Global Tech — showcased work in medtech, biotechnology, defence technology and industrial IoT. Separately, the Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society signed an agreement with Ideabaaz to give selected state deeptech startups a showcase on Ideabaaz Season 2.

The summit, in its 29th edition and held from November 17 to 19 at the Bengaluru International Exhibition Centre, also released a report putting Karnataka's global capability centres at 1,088 — 51% of the 2,117 centres in India — with 1.11 lakh AI and machine-learning professionals in the state. For Karnataka, the policy ambition running through the week is to be known not only as a technology-services centre, but as a place where emerging technologies are developed and commercialised.

The summit's own scale underlines why investors use it as a showcase: organisers reported 162 sessions, 24 roundtables and 704 speakers across the three days, with 11,257 conference delegates, 58,872 registered industry visitors and total attendance of 70,129 including students. A total of 1,518 exhibitors, including 923 startups from 104 cities, displayed products and technologies, and the event recorded 938 direct business-to-business meetings.
